identity.title: Sub-millimetre non-contaminated detection of the disc around TWA 7 by ALMA
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we present ALMA Cycle 3 Band 7 observations of the debris disk around the M2 star TWA 7

evidence.quote: one of the closest ($34.029 \pm 0.076$ pc, (cite: Gaia2018)) and youngest low-mass stars with a debris disk

question.value: Is the sub-mm emission near TWA 7 from its debris disk or a contaminant, and can the SED be explained by a single dust belt?

evidence.quote: We show that most of the emission at wavelengths longer than $\sim 300$ $\mu$m is in fact arising from a contaminant source
TWA 7 was observed twice with ALMA (project 2015.1.01015.S, PI: Bayo)
in Band 7 (346 GHz), using two different configurations

analysis_steps.goal: Subtract contaminant and measure disk flux

method.value: Fit 2D Gaussian to contaminant in uv-plane, subtract, re-image with taper, integrate emission above 2 sigma

evidence.quote: we model it as a 2D Gaussian in u-v space using the `uvmodelfit` task within CASA

validation.value: confirm emission is not an imaging artifact of the nearby contaminant

evidence.quote: To confirm that this extended emission component at the location of the star is not an artifact of imaging

method.value: Fit SED with one belt, r0=25 au and alpha_in=5 fixed, free alpha_out, s_min, composition; dust mass from least-squares scaling

evidence.quote: we fix its reference radius $r_0 = 25.0$ au
with $p$ fixed to $-3.5$ following (cite: Dohnanyi1969), with fixed $s_{\mathrm{max}} = 5$ mm
we used the astro-silicates optical constant from (cite: Draine2003)

fitting.value: emcee, 20 walkers, 1000 burn-in, 2000 step chain, uniform priors

evidence.quote: with $20$ “walkers”, a burn-in phase of $1,000$ steps, and a final chain of $2,000$ steps
We obtained an acceptance ratio of $0.44$

method.value: Solve beta + beta_wind = 0.5 at s_min with assumed wind speed 400 km/s

evidence.quote: We find that $\beta + \beta_{\mathrm{wind}} = 0.5$ can be reached for a size of $\sim 0.16$ $\mu$m
(assumed to be $400$ km.s$^{-1}$)
Both datasets were reduced using CASA (version 4.7, (cite: McMullin2007))
we used the affine invariant ensemble sampler (`emcee`, (cite: Foreman-Mackey2012))
